raw_transcript: Doctor: What brings you in today? Patient: I've had a cough and some chest tightness for about a week. Doctor: Any fever or shortness of breath? Patient: Low grade fever, no real shortness of breath. Doctor: Any history of asthma or COPD? Patient: No. Doctor: Let's listen to your lungs. I hear some mild wheezing on the right side. We'll start you on an inhaler and follow up in a week if it doesn't improve.

soap_note.subjective: Patient reports a one week history of cough and chest tightness with low grade fever. Denies shortness of breath. No history of asthma or COPD.
soap_note.objective: Mild wheezing auscultated on the right lung field. Vital signs stable.
soap_note.assessment: Acute bronchitis, likely viral, with mild reactive airway component.
soap_note.plan: Start albuterol inhaler as needed. Recommend rest and fluids. Follow up in one week if symptoms persist or worsen.

raw_transcript: Doctor: How have your blood sugars been running? Patient: Mostly in the 150 to 180 range in the mornings. Doctor: Are you still taking metformin twice a day? Patient: Yes, and I've been trying to walk more. Doctor: Good. Your A1C today is 7.8, a slight improvement from last visit. Let's continue the current dose and recheck in three months. Also let's check your cholesterol today.

soap_note.subjective: Patient with type 2 diabetes reports morning glucose readings of 150 to 180. Compliant with metformin twice daily and increased physical activity.
soap_note.objective: Hemoglobin A1C 7.8 percent, improved from prior visit. Vital signs within normal limits.
soap_note.assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, improving glycemic control.
soap_note.plan: Continue metformin at current dose. Obtain lipid panel today. Reinforce diet and exercise. Recheck A1C in three months.

raw_transcript: Doctor: What's going on today? Patient: I've had lower back pain for about three days after lifting boxes at work. Doctor: Any numbness or tingling down your legs? Patient: No, just a dull ache in my lower back. Doctor: Let's examine you. No tenderness over the spine, some muscle tightness on the left side. I don't see any red flag signs. We'll treat this as a muscle strain.

soap_note.subjective: Patient reports three days of lower back pain following a lifting injury at work. Denies radiating pain, numbness, or tingling.
soap_note.objective: No spinal tenderness. Mild left paraspinal muscle tightness. Normal gait and reflexes.
soap_note.assessment: Acute lumbar muscle strain, no red flag findings.
soap_note.plan: Recommend over the counter NSAIDs, heat therapy, and activity modification. Return if symptoms worsen or if numbness or weakness develops.

raw_transcript: Doctor: How are you sleeping and how has your mood been? Patient: Not great. I've been having trouble sleeping and feeling down most days for the past month. Doctor: Any thoughts of harming yourself? Patient: No, nothing like that. Doctor: Any major life changes recently? Patient: I lost my job last month. Doctor: That's a significant stressor. Let's talk through some options including counseling and possibly medication.

soap_note.subjective: Patient reports one month of depressed mood and insomnia following recent job loss. Denies suicidal ideation.
soap_note.objective: Alert, oriented, appropriate affect. No acute distress observed during visit.
soap_note.assessment: Major depressive disorder, single episode, likely situational, related to recent job loss.
soap_note.plan: Refer to counseling. Discuss options for pharmacologic treatment at next visit if symptoms persist. Screen again with PHQ-9 in two weeks.

raw_transcript: Doctor: How's your blood pressure been at home? Patient: I've been checking it, usually around 145 over 90. Doctor: Are you still on lisinopril? Patient: Yes, ten milligrams daily. Doctor: Given your readings, let's increase the dose to twenty milligrams and recheck in a month. Also let's review your diet, particularly sodium intake.

soap_note.subjective: Patient with hypertension reports home blood pressure readings averaging 145 over 90 while on lisinopril 10 mg daily.
soap_note.objective: Blood pressure in clinic 148 over 92. No peripheral edema.
soap_note.assessment: Essential hypertension, inadequately controlled on current dose.
soap_note.plan: Increase lisinopril to 20 mg daily. Counsel on sodium restriction. Recheck blood pressure in one month.
